title: Sanger Tree of Life HMW DNA Extraction: Manual Plant MagAttract v.2/3
author: Maja Todorovic

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer Master Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a lysis buffer master mix containing the following components:

substeps.instruction: Combine 200 µL Phosphate buffered solution (PBS)
Add 20 µL Proteinase K
Add 4 µL RNase A
Add 150 µL Buffer AL

steps.title: Sample Preparation
steps.instruction: Transfer 50 mg of cryogenically disrupted plant/fungi tissue from each sample to 2 mL microcentrifuge tubes and keep on dry ice to maintain frozen state.

steps.title: Lysis and Homogenization
steps.instruction: Add 374 µL of the lysis buffer master mix to each sample and homogenize by gently pipetting 10 times with a wide-bore pipette tip.

steps.title: Incubation
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge tubes in a mini-centrifuge to collect contents, then incubate on a heat block at 55 °C at 600 rpm for 1 hour.

steps.title: Lysate Recovery
steps.instruction: After lysis, briefly centrifuge tubes in a mini-centrifuge to spin down. Using a wide-bore pipette tip set to 380 µL, transfer the lysate to individual microcentrifuge tubes, avoiding insoluble material.

steps.title: Bead Binding
steps.instruction: Add 280 µL Buffer MB and 15 µL of Suspension G beads to each sample.

substeps.instruction: Invert the tube 10–20 times to suspend beads in the lysate
Allow 5 minutes for binding
Briefly centrifuge samples in a mini-centrifuge to collect at the bottom

steps.title: Bead Migration and Supernatant Removal
steps.instruction: Place tubes on the magnetic rack for 2–5 minutes (longer for viscous samples) for beads to migrate, then remove and discard the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Remove tubes from magnetic rack and add 700 µL Buffer MW1 directly to the bead pellet
Invert tube 10–20 times to suspend beads
Place tubes on magnetic rack for 2–5 minutes for beads to migrate
Remove and discard the supernatant
Remove tubes from magnetic rack and add 700 µL Buffer PE directly to the bead pellet
Invert tube 10–20 times to resuspend beads
Place tubes on magnetic rack for 2–5 minutes for beads to migrate
Remove and discard the supernatant

steps.title: Residual Buffer Removal
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge tubes in a mini-centrifuge and place back on the magnetic rack. Use a small micropipette to remove any residual wash buffer.

substeps.instruction: While tubes are on the magnetic rack, pipette 700 µL nuclease-free water onto the side opposite of the beads (do not pipette directly onto the pellet)
Incubate for exactly 1 minute
Slowly aspirate and discard the water

steps.title: DNA Elution - First Fraction
steps.instruction: Elute the first fraction of gDNA.

substeps.instruction: Remove samples from magnetic rack and add 200 µL of Buffer AE directly to the bead pellet
Mix by gently flicking or using a wide-bore pipette tip to dislodge the pellet
Incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature, mixing gently halfway through and at the end
Briefly centrifuge (spin down) in a mini-centrifuge and place on a magnetic rack for 2–5 minutes for bead migration
Using a 200 μL wide-bore pipette tip, carefully transfer the supernatant to a fresh microcentrifuge tube

steps.title: DNA Elution - Second Fraction
steps.instruction: Elute the second fraction of gDNA.

substeps.instruction: Remove the sample from the magnetic rack and add 200 μL Buffer AE to the bead pellet
Incubate at 25 °C, shaking at 1000 rpm, for three minutes
Centrifuge the tube briefly in a mini-centrifuge and place on a magnetic rack for 2–5 minutes for beads to migrate
Using a wide-bore pipette tip, carefully transfer the supernatant to the same microcentrifuge tube used in the first elution

steps.title: Storage
steps.instruction: Store the extracted gDNA sample at 4 °C.
